name: Test Point Planner
blurb: test point list for critical nets and probe access checks
intro: Paste the nets; each is classified (power, ground, debug, clock, high-speed, analog, control, signal) by the kind you give or by its name, and gets a priority and a test-point count. With positions, the pads are checked for probe pitch, board-edge distance and side, using common in-circuit-test DFT guidance.

usage: Paste nets one per line as NAME [kind] [current A] [@x,y in mm] [top|bottom] (or a KiCad netlist), and pick the method (bed, flying, pogo, manual). It returns a per-net plan (kind, must/should/optional/avoid, number of test points, why), the ground test-point count, the pad size, pitch and edge rules for the method, access problems for placed pads, and a TP list text. Use it before layout to reserve test points, or after placement to check probe access.
sources: In-circuit test DFT guidance (Keysight/Agilent ICT fixture design guidelines): 100 mil pitch, 0.9-1.0 mm pads, 0.125 in from board edge
Flying-probe and pogo-fixture pad sizes: common fixture-maker rules of thumb
